title: Correct net force calculation
description: Essential: Student correctly computes the net horizontal force as F1 - F2 = 7 N.

title: Friction magnitude for part (1)
description: Essential: Student states the static friction force equals the net force of 7 N, as it is less than the maximum static friction.

title: Friction direction for part (1)
description: Important: Student identifies the friction direction opposes the net applied force, correctly stating it is to the left.

title: Friction after removing F1
description: Essential: For part (2), student finds the static friction force equals the remaining applied force F2 = 6 N, opposing it to the right.

title: Comparison to maximum friction
description: Important: Student compares the required static friction force to the maximum (8 N) to determine if the block moves or not.

title: Kinetic friction for part (3)
description: Essential: For part (3), student correctly identifies the block moves and the friction is kinetic, with magnitude μN = 8 N.

title: Direction for kinetic friction
description: Important: Student states the kinetic friction direction opposes the motion/remaining applied force (F1), which is to the left.

title: Confusing static and kinetic
description: Pitfall: Student incorrectly uses kinetic friction when the block is in static equilibrium (parts 1 & 2).

title: Sign or direction error
description: Pitfall: Student makes an error in the sign/direction of the net force or friction force for any part.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Student includes correct units (N) for all force magnitudes.
